utility.notes: PG&E's own official service-area documentation describes its Northern/Central California electric and gas service territory as including San Joaquin County, where Stockton is the county seat.

value.notes: Ava Community Energy's own official FAQ page directly confirms it serves Stockton, alongside other San Joaquin County cities (Lathrop, Tracy) and most of Alameda County. PG&E remains the distribution/billing utility; customers may opt out back to PG&E generation.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by PG&E across its entire distribution territory, which includes Stockton/San Joaquin County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC/PG&E-administered SGIP program and figures already confirmed for the San Jose/Fremont/Oakland/Fresno records, reused on the same reasoning: SGIP is administered per IOU distribution territory (PG&E), not per city. 'Available through 2025' read as expiring 2025-12-31, before last_verified, hence 'expired'; the other tier's status is 'unknown' since no end/current-status is stated. Re-check against selfgenca.com's live Program Metrics page before showing as current. Removed the previously-listed "SGIP - Equity Resiliency" line item on 2026-08-09: its expires_on (2025-12-31) has definitively elapsed and no renewal/replacement was confirmed this session, so it no longer represents a current program; the remaining item(s) here are still active/unknown-status per their own status field.

value.name: Standard plan and checklist of all requirements, published on the City's website, substantially conforming to the California Solar Permitting Guidebook

required_documents.notes: Per Stockton Municipal Code Section 15.78.040(A),(D)-(E): the Building Department adopts a standard plan and checklist substantially conforming to the CA Solar Permitting Guidebook, made available on the City's website. The City's own SolarAPP+ / 'Residential Solar One Stop' online application (S1) is the modern submission channel for eligible systems.

value: Only one inspection shall be required for eligible small residential rooftop solar energy systems (a separate fire inspection may apply absent a local fire-authority agreement); an inspection will be scheduled within two business days of a request and provide a two-hour inspection window
The inspection shall be done in a timely manner and should include consolidated inspections
If a system fails inspection, a subsequent inspection is authorized

value.notes: Stockton Municipal Code Section 15.78.050(A): the Building Department shall issue a permit '(the same day for over-the-counter applications or within one to three business days for electronic applications)' of receipt of a complete application. Directly confirmed this session via the City's own municipal code, replacing the prior lower-confidence (0.6), search-engine-derived 'instant issuance' claim with this more specific, code-based figure.

value.program_or_pathway: Small Residential Rooftop Solar Energy Systems expedited permitting (Stockton Municipal Code Chapter 15.78), submitted via the City's SolarAPP+/Residential Solar One Stop online application
other_conditions: System must be installed on a single- or duplex-family dwelling
Solar panel/module array must not exceed the maximum legal building height as defined by the authority having jurisdiction

permit_fees.notes: Not stated in any source reviewed this session.

rebates.notes: No Stockton-specific rebate program found this session, distinct from the statewide SGIP battery incentives already recorded under battery_programs.
